task_spec: SUBJECT: pin the reconnect commands' observable behaviour in the byte-level parity oracle, and make the oracle itself tamper-evident, BEFORE any shared-core refactor begins

scope: tests/baselines/manifest.json, tests/baselines/regenerate.py, tests/fixtures/build_fixtures.py (fixture additions only), a new tests/test_parity_baseline.py, an annotated git tag parity-baseline-v1
out-of-scope: any change under traktor_nml/ (production code) - this commit is test/fixture only
out-of-scope: the result-object/renderer split, on_progress callback, cancel token, fpcalc direct-Popen change - all land AFTER this commit
out-of-scope: any GUI code; the NiceGUI package does not exist yet
out-of-scope: CI workflow authoring beyond stating the required check (repo has no CI config today - confirm during explore)
constraints: MUST NOT change production behaviour; if manifest.json regeneration produces a diff for the pre-existing 8 cases, that is a defect in this change, not a new baseline
MUST keep every new baseline case deterministic across runs, machines and temp dirs - the oracle compares stdout byte-for-byte
MUST add cases for scan-reconnect-candidates and rewrite-from-reconnect covering: a --dry-run form, a writing form, an ambiguous-match case, a dangling-match case
SHOULD add one fingerprint-tier case driven by a stub fpcalc on PATH, so the later direct-Popen change is covered by the oracle rather than only unit tests
MUST add tests/test_parity_baseline.py asserting a PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 constant against the manifest's hash, runnable under plain pytest with no git dependency
MUST add a meta-test proving the guard FAILS on a one-character mutation (mirrors existing test_deliberate_one_character_edit_fails_parity)
MUST tag the resulting commit parity-baseline-v1 (annotated, pushed)
SHOULD keep pytest suite green: pytest tests/ -q
entry_points: tests/baselines/regenerate.py:CASES - the argv list to extend; also _OUTPUT_ARG_INDEX which maps a command to its output-path argument (rewrite-from-reconnect needs an entry: output is argv[2])
tests/baselines/regenerate.py:regenerate - chdirs into a temp dir, runs main(argv) in-process, captures stdout/stderr/exit_code and base64 of every output file
tests/test_baseline_parity.py - the consumer; parametrised over manifest cases, asserts exit code, stdout and written bytes

tests/fixtures/build_fixtures.py:build_fixtures - already writes stub .mp3 files (xtal.mp3, roygbiv_final.mp3, archangel_128/320.mp3, cafe.mp3, baby.mp3, come_on.mp3) so corpus/ can serve as a --scan-root
tests/conftest.py:run_tool - in-process invocation used by the rest of the suite
traktor_nml/commands/reconnect_cmd.py:_run_reconnection - resolves volume identity then indexes scan roots
traktor_nml/tagcache.py:TagCache - cache is keyed path|size|mtime and flushes every 50 puts; written even under --dry-run
traktor_nml/fingerprint.py:_compute_fingerprint - calls acoustid.fingerprint_file; HAS_ACOUSTID gates the tier
rejected_alternatives: git diff --exit-code on manifest.json as the CI gate - rejected: passes on any commit that regenerated AND committed the baseline, which is exactly the case it must catch (this is why 3.1a exists)

Relying only on unit tests for the reconnect cores - rejected: the oracle pins stdout and written bytes, which is what the renderer split must preserve; unit tests would be written against the new shape and could not detect drift from the old
Regenerating manifest.json during the refactor to make a failing test pass - rejected as the defining anti-pattern; regeneration is only correct for a reviewed, deliberate behaviour change
Committing the reconnect cases after the refactor - rejected: the oracle must predate the change it is meant to police
current_understanding: manifest.json currently holds 8 cases across 7 subcommands: inspect x2, encode-dir, preview-diff, rewrite, preview-compare, scan-compare-candidates, rewrite-from-collection-compare
It covers NONE of scan-reconnect-candidates, rewrite-from-reconnect, splice, split, build-playlist, discover-tracks, discover-collection-tracks
regenerate.py is the only sanctioned way to update the manifest; it is deterministic because the fixture corpus and the argv list are both fixed

Determinism risk 1 (HIGH): reconnect resolves and prints filesystem paths. regenerate() chdirs into a per-run temp dir, so any absolute path reaching stdout embeds that temp dir and makes the baseline unreproducible. Must be established empirically before choosing cases.
Determinism risk 2: TagCache keys include st_mtime of the stub mp3s, which differ per run. The cache file is a side file, not an output_files entry, but any cache stat printed to stdout could vary.
Determinism risk 3: scan-root indexing order may depend on filesystem enumeration order.
Determinism risk 4: resolve_volume_identity may raise VolumeIdentityError when the prefix scan is ambiguous, in which case --volume-map must be supplied explicitly to keep the case stable.

Determinism risk 5 (fingerprint case): a stub fpcalc must be deterministic and reachable; HAS_ACOUSTID depends on pyacoustid being importable, which may not hold in every environment - the case may need to be skipped rather than baselined if the dependency is optional.
assumptions: build_fixtures' stub .mp3 files are not real audio, so mutagen tag reads fail and matching falls back to filename/path evidence - still deterministic (M)
The repo has no CI workflow today, so the CI half of 3.1a will be documented rather than implemented in this commit (M - verify during explore)
pyacoustid/fpcalc are absent on this machine, so the fingerprint-tier baseline case will need a stub binary on PATH or must be deferred (M)
Adding cases to CASES and regenerating will not perturb the 8 existing entries, since each case runs in the same fresh temp dir and order is stable (H)
A new fixture may be needed to produce a genuinely ambiguous reconnect match; duplicate_rips.nml is the likeliest existing candidate (M)
invisible_knowledge: DL-002/DL-011: the manifest records stdout, exit code and written bytes as the tool's behavioural contract; regenerating it to go green silently rewrites that contract
The oracle's value is that it predates the change it polices - committing it after the refactor proves nothing
The tag cache is deliberately written even under --dry-run because it is a scan speedup, not the command's output; this exception is documented in README and must not be 'fixed' here

Accepted tradeoff: parity-baseline-v1 cannot be server-side protected (GitHub rulesets need Pro or a public repo; the legacy tags/protection API is gone). A local pre-push hook at .git/hooks/pre-push refuses to move or delete parity-baseline-* tags; the authoritative pin is the pytest hash constant, which does not depend on the tag.

Because the tag is only hook-protected, any CI job that diffs against parity-baseline-v1 must ALSO assert the tag still resolves to its recorded commit SHA - otherwise a moved tag moves the comparison with it
Phase 1 of the GUI work is the reconnect wizard only; these two commands are exactly the ones the first refactor touches, which is why they are task 0 rather than a general coverage sweep
